data.long_meaning: The name Atigay is derived from Sanskrit words 'ati' meaning 'beyond' and 'gaya' meaning 'boundaries'. This name signifies one who transcends all limits and barriers. This name is a symbol of limitless potential and fearless exploration.

historical_references.reference: Atigay was a celebrated Hindu king of the Chalukya Dynasty, who ruled from 1138 to 1154 CE. He is remembered for his military conquests, particularly his defeat of the Hoysalas at the Battle of Talikota in 1137 CE.
historical_references.context: Chalukya Dynasty, Military conquests, Battle of Talikota

historical_references.reference: Atigay, also known as Bhillama II, was a king of the Yadava Dynasty in the Deccan region of India. He ruled from 1236 to 1242 CE and is known for his patronage of literature and arts, particularly the Jain scholar Hemacandra.
